summary: Concurrent tool confirmation race during hot-restart causes duplicate external side-effects for Python SDK multiplexed sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external webhook posts and duplicate records in their downstream DB after a Redwood service hot-restart while using the Python SDK with multiplexed websocket sessions. The duplication only occurs when two tool (funcall) invocations are in-flight concurrently on the same multiplexed session and a host performing a hot-restart races with confirmation acknowledgements.

Impact:
- Customer observed duplicate side-effects (double webhook POSTs) for ~0.4% of requests during a rolling hot-restart last night.
- Affects business-critical billing pipeline at Novara Health (dedicated tenant).
- Customer requests urgent mitigation and a root-cause analysis.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Region: prod-us-east
- SDK: python-sdk v0.12.4 (ws multiplexing enabled)
- Serving runtime: 2.8.1
- Router version: 1.14.0 with hot-restart enabled
- Observed on model: redwood-open-instruct-1

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied, reliably reproduces in their staging):
1) Establish a multiplexed websocket session from python-sdk with session-id header X-Session-ID: example-abc-001.
2) Send two concurrent funcall requests A and B through the same session (A triggers an external webhook; B is a short metadata lookup).
3) Trigger a hot-restart on the worker serving that session (simulated by restart command or rolling deploy).
4) Observe: worker1 queues acknowledgements while migrating session state; worker2 accepts reconnect and the SDK resends confirmations; worker1 later emits a delayed ACK for A, server-side retry path treats it as a separate confirmation and re-enqueues the outgoing webhook.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate webhook POSTs with identical payloads (timestamps differ by ~150–400ms).
- SDK client logs show reconnect + resend logic followed by a delayed ack from the original connection.
- Server trace shows two separate tool-confirmation events for the same idempotency key due to inconsistent in-memory state during handoff.

Expected behavior:
- Tool confirmations should be deduplicated across worker handoff; idempotency key or confirmation token should be canonicalized and honored to avoid duplicate side-effects.

Initial hypothesis:
- Hot-restart migration flow leaves a small window where the old worker can emit confirmations after the router has switched the canonical session to a new worker. The confirmation deduplication is currently per-worker in-memory and not globally coordinated, causing both workers to signal success independently.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated customer logs with platform traces (trace ids included below) show Worker-A (10.12.4.21) emitted a delayed confirmation event 220ms after connection close. Router log shows session reassigned to Worker-B (10.12.4.78) which processed the retransmitted confirmation first.
- Sample trace ids: trace-0a7f3c9b, trace-0a7f3d1f, request-id: r-7c3b2f44.
- Confirmation tokens observed in logs: conf_tok: 3f9b-xyz-77 and conf_tok: 3f9b-xyz-77 (same token) — but deduplication keys in the runtime were keyed by worker-local ack index, not the full confirmation token.
- Reproduction in a local cluster using python-sdk v0.12.4 + serving-runtime 2.8.1 shows same duplication when enabling graceful hot-restart.

Logs (redacted):
- Worker-A (old): [2026-03-11T22:14:02.198Z] conn-close session=example-abc-001; pending-acks=[A,B]; emit-confirm A conf_tok=3f9b-xyz-77
- Router: [2026-03-11T22:14:02.310Z] session-move session=example-abc-001 -> 10.12.4.78
- Worker-B (new): [2026-03-11T22:14:02.355Z] recv-confirm A conf_tok=3f9b-xyz-77; enqueue-outgoing-webhook id=w-9931
- Worker-A (delayed): [2026-03-11T22:14:02.418Z] late-confirm A conf_tok=3f9b-xyz-77; enqueue-outgoing-webhook id=w-9932

Workaround / temporary mitigation implemented:
- Support recommended disabling hot-restart for Novara Health's autoscaler (temporary) which reduced duplicate events to 0 in last 3h.
- Customer applied SDK-side mitigation: use single in-flight funcall per session (serializing calls) as a short-term measure.

Long-term remediation ideas (engineering):
1) Global confirmation-dedup store: persist recent confirmation tokens to a small distributed cache (etcd/redis) keyed by tenant+confirmation-token to dedupe across workers during migration.
2) Router-level stall: when migrating session, have router buffer delayed confirmations for a short grace window and drop duplicates based on token canonicalization.
3) SDK acknowledgement change: include monotonically increasing session-confirm-id that the server can use to detect stale worker acknowledgements.

Next steps / action items:
- SRE/Runtime to reproduce in canary with instrumentation and confirm race window. (Assigned to runtime team).
- Implement short-term router stall + in-memory canonicalization (prototype PR linked).
- Notify customer of expected timeline for fix; keep hot-restart disabled for their dedicated pool until patch: ETA 2026-03-20 for canary rollout.

Resolution notes (current):
- No permanent fix yet; temporary workaround (disable hot-restart) accepted by customer.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage completed with customer. They provided staging repro steps and logs. Escalated to runtime team.
2026-03-12 - Riley Thompson (SRE): Reproduced locally using customer's repro harness. Confirmed race between worker handoff and delayed ack. Added runtime tracing to capture ack token path.
2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel (Runtime Eng): Hypothesis: per-worker local dedupe key is insufficient. Will prototype router buffering + token canonicalization. Assigned to PR 1246 for serving-runtime.
2026-03-13 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed temporary mitigation (disabled hot-restart) stopped duplicates in production window. They'll keep mitigation in place until patch is rolled out.
2026-03-13 - Riley Thompson (SRE): Created canary plan and rollout schedule. Target canary start 2026-03-18. Will update ticket with test results and postmortem link once complete.
resolution: Investigating. Temporary mitigation: hot-restart disabled for customer's dedicated pool and SDK-side serializing of funcalls. Engineering to prototype router buffering and global confirmation dedupe; ETA for canary: 2026-03-18, full rollout pending successful canary.
